concepts.name: FTA vs PTA vs CECA vs CEPA: Definitional Distinctions
key_dimensions: Precise definitional differences between FTA, PTA (Preferential Trade Agreement), CECA (Comprehensive Economic Cooperation Agreement), and CEPA (Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement)
Which India agreements fall under which category — UPSC trap: India-Sri Lanka is a PTA, India-UAE is a CEPA
Scope comparison: goods-only FTAs vs CEPAs covering services, investment, and IPR
WTO legal basis: Article XXIV of GATT for FTAs vs Enabling Clause for PTAs

concepts.name: Rules of Origin (RoO) in India's FTAs
key_dimensions: Definition and purpose: preventing trade deflection and misuse of concessional tariffs
Key criteria: substantial transformation, value-addition threshold, change in tariff heading (CTH)
India-ASEAN FTA controversy: low value-addition norms allegedly allowing Chinese goods re-routing through ASEAN
RoO tightening as a non-tariff measure and its role in review of existing FTAs

concepts.name: India-ASEAN FTA: Structure, Outcomes, and Criticisms
key_dimensions: Signed 2009 (goods), services and investment agreements in 2014 — scope and coverage
Trade deficit widening post-FTA: India's deficit with ASEAN grew significantly, raising concerns about domestic industry
Sectors excluded or sensitive-listed: India kept agriculture, dairy, and certain manufacturing on exclusion/sensitive lists
Review negotiations initiated: reasons including RoO weaknesses, non-tariff barriers by ASEAN, and asymmetric liberalization

concepts.name: India-UAE CEPA: Significance and Firsts
key_dimensions: Concluded in record ~90 days (2022) — significance as India's fastest-negotiated FTA and first CEPA in a decade
Coverage: goods, services, investment, government procurement — making it a comprehensive agreement
Key gains: tariff elimination on 97% Indian goods, market access for Indian services (IT, healthcare, professional services)
Strategic dimension: stepping stone for India-GCC FTA and reducing dependence on oil imports through trade balancing

concepts.name: India-UK FTA Negotiations: Key Sticking Points
key_dimensions: India's offensive interests: Mode 4 movement of professionals, services liberalization, reduction of Scotch whisky tariffs by UK ask vs India's sensitivity
UK's offensive interests: lower tariffs on automobiles, Scotch whisky, financial services market access
Contentious issues: India's data localization norms, UK's social security contributions (totalization agreement linkage), and carbon border adjustment mechanism (CBAM) implications
Geopolitical context: post-Brexit UK seeking new trade partners; India leveraging its large market size

concepts.name: India's Decision to Stay Out of RCEP: Rationale and Implications
key_dimensions: RCEP (Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership): 15-nation agreement covering ~30% of global GDP — India opted out in 2019
India's stated concerns: trade deficit fears (especially with China), weak RoO, inadequate services liberalization, and threat to domestic dairy and agriculture
Economic implications: India missing out on regional value chains, FDI diversion to RCEP members
Strategic implications: signal of 'Atmanirbhar' orientation vs. arguments that staying out increases isolation from Asian supply chains

concepts.name: India-Sri Lanka Free Trade Agreement (ISFTA): India's Oldest FTA
key_dimensions: Signed 1998, operational 2000 — India's first bilateral FTA, technically a PTA covering only goods
Negative lists: both sides maintain lists of excluded products; India's includes key agricultural items
Trade deflection controversy: copper and vanaspati re-export through Sri Lanka exploiting concessional tariffs
Stalled expansion into ECTA (Economic and Technology Cooperation Agreement): reasons including Sri Lanka's economic crisis and political factors

concepts.name: India-South Korea CEPA: Benchmark and Lessons
key_dimensions: Signed 2009 — India's first CEPA, seen as a template for future comprehensive agreements
Outcome asymmetry: India's trade deficit with South Korea widened post-CEPA, raising questions about negotiating capacity
Services liberalization gains: Indian IT professionals and companies benefited, but goods deficit dominated discourse
Under review since 2016: illustrates systemic issue of India renegotiating FTAs due to poor initial outcome assessment

concepts.name: India-Japan CEPA: Strategic and Economic Dimensions
key_dimensions: Signed 2011 — covers goods, services, investment, and cooperation in areas like IP and competition policy
Utilization rate problem: Indian exporters under-utilize concessions due to complex RoO compliance and lack of awareness — a recurring FTA challenge
Japan's investment in India: CEPA as a platform that accompanied significant Japanese FDI (Delhi-Mumbai Industrial Corridor linkage)
Review underway: upgrading CEPA to reflect changed trade patterns and new sectors like digital trade

concepts.name: FTA Utilization Rate: India's Systemic Challenge
key_dimensions: Definition: percentage of eligible exports/imports actually claiming preferential tariff rates under an FTA
India's low utilization rates (often below 25% for some FTAs) vs. ASEAN countries' rates above 60%
Causes: complex RoO compliance costs, lack of exporter awareness, cumbersome certification processes, and preference margins too small to justify compliance costs
Policy responses: single-window systems, FTA cells in DGFT, capacity building for MSMEs as potential exporters

concepts.name: Trade in Services under India's FTAs: The Four Modes
key_dimensions: GATS framework: Mode 1 (cross-border supply), Mode 2 (consumption abroad), Mode 3 (commercial presence), Mode 4 (movement of natural persons) — FTAs go beyond GATS commitments
India's core interest: Mode 4 liberalization (IT professionals, healthcare workers) — often blocked by partner countries citing immigration sensitivities
Mode 3 sensitivities for India: resisting foreign commercial presence in retail, legal, financial services
Negative list vs. positive list approach: India preferring negative list (more liberalization, fewer exclusions) in services chapters of recent FTAs

concepts.name: Investor-State Dispute Settlement (ISDS) in India's FTAs
key_dimensions: ISDS mechanism: allows foreign investors to sue host governments in international tribunals (ICSID, UNCITRAL)
India's experience: multiple ISDS claims (Vodafone, Cairn Energy, White Industries) costing India billions — triggered model BIT revision in 2016
India's Model BIT 2016: narrowed definition of investment, excluded taxation and compulsory licensing from ISDS, mandated exhaustion of domestic remedies for 5 years before international arbitration
Impact on FTA negotiations: India's reluctance to include ISDS chapters; tension with partners (EU, UK) demanding investor protection

concepts.name: India's FTA Negotiating Capacity and Institutional Framework
key_dimensions: Nodal ministry: Ministry of Commerce and Industry (DGFT + Trade Policy Division) leads FTA negotiations
Inter-ministerial consultation gap: MEA, Finance, Agriculture, and sectoral ministries often inadequately consulted, leading to post-signing controversies
Comparison with EU's negotiating model: EU has a single Trade Commissioner and mandate-based negotiation; India's fragmented structure causes delays and inconsistency
Recent reform: establishment of Trade Policy Forum mechanisms and think-tank integration (GTRI, ICRIER) for pre-negotiation impact assessments

concepts.name: Non-Tariff Barriers (NTBs) and Their Interaction with FTAs
key_dimensions: Types of NTBs: Sanitary and Phytosanitary (SPS) measures, Technical Barriers to Trade (TBT), import licensing, and customs procedures
Paradox: India's FTAs reduce tariffs, but partners' NTBs (especially in agriculture and processed food) negate market access gains for India
India's own NTBs: BIS certification requirements, mandatory testing, labeling norms — used as defensive instruments but also seen as protectionist
NTB chapters in modern FTAs: India pushing for NTB elimination alongside tariff reduction in recent negotiations (India-EU FTA)

concepts.name: India-EU FTA (BTIA) Negotiations: Deadlock and Revival
key_dimensions: BTIA (Broad-based Trade and Investment Agreement): negotiations launched 2007, stalled 2013, relaunched 2022

Key sticking points: India's resistance to IP chapter (TRIPS-plus provisions, data exclusivity affecting pharma generics), EU's demand for carbon border adjustment compatibility, and geographical indications (GI) protection
EU's new asks: sustainability chapter (labor standards, environmental commitments), digital trade, and public procurement market access
Strategic importance: EU is India's largest trading partner collectively; agreement could be transformative but complexity makes it India's most challenging negotiation

concepts.name: Intellectual Property Rights (IPR) in FTA Negotiations: India's Defensive Interests
key_dimensions: TRIPS-plus provisions in FTAs: patent term extensions, data exclusivity, evergreening — demanded by US/EU, resisted by India to protect generic pharma industry
India's Section 3(d) of Patents Act: prevents evergreening; EU/US FTAs would potentially challenge this provision
GI protection in FTAs: India seeks protection for Indian GIs (Darjeeling tea, Basmati rice) while resisting European GIs displacing Indian products
Copyright term extension demands: US pushing for 70-year copyright term vs. India's TRIPS-compliant 60-year term — an FTA pressure point

concepts.name: India's FTAs and the Domestic Industry Impact: Trade Diversion vs. Trade Creation
key_dimensions: Trade creation: FTAs shift production to more efficient partner — beneficial; Trade diversion: shifts from efficient non-member to less efficient member due to tariff preference — welfare-reducing
India's experience: concerns that FTAs with ASEAN and South Korea created trade diversion favoring Chinese goods via third countries, not genuine trade creation
Sector-specific impacts: Indian textiles, electronics, and steel faced import surges post-FTAs; MSME sector particularly vulnerable
Economic Survey analysis: India's FTA trade balance is negative with most FTA partners, fueling protectionist political economy arguments against new agreements

concepts.name: Digital Trade Provisions in India's Emerging FTA Framework
key_dimensions: Definition: rules governing e-commerce, data flows, digital services, source code protection, and customs duties on digital transmissions
India's moratorium position: India opposes permanent moratorium on customs duties on electronic transmissions at WTO/FTAs, arguing revenue loss and policy space concerns
Data localization vs. free data flow: India's DPDP Act and RBI data localization norms conflict with partner demands for cross-border data flow commitments in FTAs
India-UAE CEPA as precedent: included a digital trade chapter — sets template but India maintains reservations on key issues like source code protection demands

concepts.name: Government Procurement Chapter in FTAs: India's Exclusion Strategy
key_dimensions: Government procurement = purchase of goods/services by government entities; covered under WTO's GPA (Government Procurement Agreement) — India is an observer, not member
India's resistance: Make in India, Atmanirbhar Bharat, and Public Procurement (Preference to Make in India) Order conflict with opening procurement to FTA partners
Partner demands: EU, UK, and US seek access to India's large public procurement market (railways, defense, infrastructure) in FTA negotiations
Selective inclusion: India-UAE CEPA included limited procurement provisions — signals India may open procurement selectively for strategic partners while maintaining general exclusion

concepts.name: FTAs and Agricultural Sensitivity: India's Exclusion and Safeguard Mechanisms
key_dimensions: India's consistent exclusion of sensitive agricultural products from FTA concessions: dairy, oilseeds, certain cereals — driven by rural livelihood and food security concerns

Special Safeguard Mechanism (SSM): allows developing countries to temporarily raise tariffs when import surges or price falls threaten domestic farmers — India advocates SSM in multilateral and bilateral contexts
RCEP agriculture concern: New Zealand and Australian dairy and meat exports feared to undermine Indian farmers — central to India's RCEP opt-out
Tension with Cairns Group partners: countries like Australia and New Zealand make agricultural market access a precondition for FTA finalization, creating deadlock with India
